clue.text: Part of foot stumped English player, initially batting first

indicators.note: says the batting piece is placed at the front of the charade

parts.note: a batsman who is batting is in
ST is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word player is taken

explanation.surface: A cricket report: an English player stumped after batting, perhaps with a sore foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' tells you the IN for 'batting' goes at the front, ahead of the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The arched upper middle section of the human foot, between toes and ankle, is a named part of it.

clue.text: Can do

definitions.meaning: to do someone is to cheat or defraud them

explanation.surface: Two words that look like an expression of willingness, as in a can-do attitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British slang: the can and the nick are prison, and to do or nick someone is to swindle them.

clue.text: Dawn French very hot inside reserve

indicators.note: the hot letter goes within the French word for very

parts.note: tres is the French word for very
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
to hold something is to reserve it, as with a table

explanation.surface: Dawn French, the comedian, keeping her cool while being very hot.
explanation.walkthrough: Dawn French is a British comic actor; here 'Dawn' alone is the definition and 'French' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, a starting point or beginning: the dawn of an era is its very edge.

clue.text: Morgan, when entertaining live, is a tool

indicators.note: to entertain is to take in a guest, so one name holds the other letter

parts.note: Piers Morgan is a British TV presenter and journalist
L stands for live, as on the wiring of a British plug

explanation.surface: A dig at a TV personality: Piers Morgan, presenting live, is a tool (slang for an idiot).
explanation.definitionFit: A gripping hand implement with two hinged jaws, used by electricians and other trades.

clue.text: Judge film — British want something extremely dark

parts.note: E.T. is the Spielberg film about an extraterrestrial
to want something is to lack it

explanation.surface: A film critic judging a British movie that lacks something, finding it extremely dark.
explanation.definitionFit: A colour term meaning deepest possible black, like the gemstone jet.

clue.text: Dad going out with hat, worn jeans and old jumper

indicators.note: a fire going out falls apart, so these letters are scattered and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A father on a date in a hat, scruffy jeans and an ancient sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' looks like a British sweater; it is an athlete. Jonathan Edwards is a retired British triple jumper, world record holder.
explanation.definitionFit: A former Olympic triple-jump champion, hence an athlete who once jumped for a living.

clue.text: Long to run into class that's coming up? Do they?

definitions.text: Long to run into class that's coming up? Do they?

indicators.note: the longing and run pieces go inside the class word
in a down clue, coming up means the word set is read bottom to top

parts.note: a set is a class or group of pupils
to ache for something is to long for it
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A question: do staff really long to rush into the next lesson?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: those who take classes, and whether they are keen to run into them.
explanation.definitionFit: Educators who take classes of pupils are the ones the clue wonders about.

clue.text: One male, totally revolting animal that might spit at you?

definitions.text: animal that might spit at you

indicators.note: in a down clue, revolting means turned upside down, so the pieces read backwards

parts.note: a means one
all means totally, as in all wrong

explanation.surface: A disgusting man spitting at people, like a camelid.
explanation.definitionFit: This South American camelid is famous for spitting at people who annoy it.

clue.text: Release for women with it? Primarily kiss fellow with tongue

parts.note: chic means stylish or with it

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word kiss is used

parts.note: to lick something is to tongue it

explanation.surface: A racy scene: a film starts with a kiss and a man using his tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Release' is a film release, not a letting go.
explanation.definitionFit: A romantic film aimed mainly at a female audience, a cinema release made for women.

clue.text: Tail of this one concerning, going over back of body

definitions.text: Tail of this one concerning, going over back of body

indicators.note: the tail is the final letter of the word this
one plus concerning goes over the last letter of the body word, replacing it

parts.note: a corps is a body of people, as in diplomatic corps
I is the Roman numeral one
on means concerning, as in a talk on art

explanation.surface: A warning: the tail of this creature is a worry, arching over its back.
explanation.walkthrough: S of 'this' starts it; the S at the end of CORPS is swapped for ION. As a whole, the clue pictures the stinging tail arching over the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The arachnid's venomous tail curls up over its back, which makes it worrying.

clue.text: Plant in America around spies

parts.note: CA, circa, means around, as with a date
the CIA is the American intelligence agency

explanation.surface: A plant in America is surrounded by agents, like a planted spy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' could be a mole among spies; it is a shrub or tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A wattle or thorn tree, a genus of flowering shrubs and trees.

clue.text: Signs of growth in tax records

parts.note: to tax something is to stretch it to its limits
marks are records, such as scores written down

explanation.surface: An accountant spotting rising income in a set of tax returns.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines left on the skin after rapid growth or pregnancy are a visible sign of the body growing.

clue.text: Supply, eg oil? No, USA is rich in oil

indicators.note: read as supple-ly, in a flexible way, so these letters are bent into a new shape

explanation.surface: An oil trader asking about supply, answered that America is rich in oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' reads as a noun; it is the adverb from supple.
explanation.definitionFit: Greasy or oily in texture; also used of fawning manner, but here literal.

clue.text: Ace place to go for Indian food

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace on playing cards
the loo is British slang for the toilet, where one goes

explanation.surface: A recommendation of a great spot to eat curry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hindi word for potato, seen on menus in dishes such as Bombay potatoes.

clue.text: One is fired: character to get sack

parts.note: an air is a character or manner, as in an air of mystery
to rifle is to plunder or sack a place

explanation.surface: An employee is dismissed: their character earns them the sack.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun using compressed gas to shoot pellets is something that gets fired.

clue.text: Drive and change oil in sump

indicators.note: an instruction to change the letters, putting them in a new order

explanation.surface: Car maintenance: drive it, then change the oil in the sump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' looks motoring; it means impulse or urge.
explanation.definitionFit: A force or urge pushing someone forward, as an inner drive does.

clue.text: Support for member to pay balance

parts.note: to foot the bill is to pay it
the rest is the balance or remainder

explanation.surface: A club member is helped to settle an outstanding account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member' looks like a club member; it is a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: A stool or rail on which to prop one's lower limb, so a support for that limb.

clue.text: Large bunches of bananas over us

parts.note: a hand is a bunch of bananas growing together
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
in British speech, us can mean me, as in give us a kiss

explanation.surface: A greengrocer's huge bunches of bananas towering over the customers.
explanation.definitionFit: As in a handsome sum or profit, meaning sizeable or generous.

clue.text: Prepare to leave group

definitions.meaning: to fill your suitcase before going away
a band of wolves or cards, a collection

explanation.surface: Someone getting ready to depart from a gang.
explanation.definitionFit: One word for filling luggage before departure and for a group, as of wolves or cub scouts.

clue.text: Personal feature of writer covering current work

indicators.note: the pen surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: a Bic is a brand of ballpoint pen, a writer
I is the physics symbol for electric current
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A journalist covering present work for a personal profile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feature' is a feature film, not a newspaper piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A film telling one person's life story, a feature about an individual.

clue.text: Try that Viagra, mostly while worried about sex

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the sex piece
worried letters are shaken about and rearranged
all of the word Viagra but its final letter

parts.note: it is a coy word for sex

explanation.surface: Encouragement to try the little blue pill despite performance nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the final A of Viagra; 'worried' scrambles the rest with while, and 'about' wraps that jumble around the sex piece. 'that' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning to have a go at something, to attempt it.

clue.text: Bottoms of wee babies are turned over for wipe

indicators.note: flipped, so the pieces read backwards
in a down clue the bottoms are the final letters of the words wee and babies

parts.note: taken as written; that the whole answer also runs backwards through 'babies are' is a coincidence, as the blog parse uses the bottoms of wee and babies

explanation.surface: Nappy changing: little babies turned over to have their bottoms cleaned.
explanation.definitionFit: To delete or rub out, as on a whiteboard, which is to wipe it clean.

clue.text: Drink up Earl Grey

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: to lap is to drink like a cat

explanation.surface: An instruction to finish a cup of Earl Grey tea.
explanation.walkthrough: Earl Grey is a tea; it is split, Earl giving E and Grey the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey as in looking wan or ill, pallid and colourless.

clue.text: Measure and cook herb

parts.note: to do food is to cook it, as in do the potatoes
sage is a culinary herb

explanation.surface: Kitchen instructions: weigh out and prepare the herb.
explanation.definitionFit: A measured amount of medicine to be taken at one time.

clue.text: Salesperson returning city gentleman's payback

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

indicators.note: going back, so the city and gentleman pieces read backwards

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
sir is a title or address for a gentleman

explanation.surface: A salesman back from a city getting his revenge on a gent.
explanation.definitionFit: Retaliation for an injury, paying someone back in kind.

clue.text: Harmful stuff when former footballer so drunk

parts.note: as means when, as in as I left
George Best was a famous Manchester United footballer, known for drinking

indicators.note: drunk letters stagger out of order

explanation.surface: A nod to George Best, a former footballer known for his heavy drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A fibrous mineral once used in insulation that causes lung disease.

clue.text: Drop sign having changed hands

indicators.note: right becomes left: the letter for right swaps for the letter for left

parts.note: Cancer is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A sign being dropped after passing to new owners.
explanation.definitionFit: To call off or abandon a plan, to drop it.
